producer_report.summary: Root cause: the reader's brief never said how many tokens each composed prompt set had left, so readings planned growth in shared prompt files (verifier, reader, producer frames) that overran a budget (3 jobs). Fix at the source: new `athena_context::headroom_rows` (lib.rs) uses `compose` and `BudgetSet::budget()` to give each set's component ids, estimated tokens, budget and tokens left (contract, reader, planner, critic, producer and verifier per enabled capability). `ReaderInputs` gained a `headroom` field; `reader_brief` renders a 'Prompt token headroom' section (absent when empty) that says an edit to a shared file costs every set that includes it. `reading.rs` builds the rows from the enabled capabilities. No budget number is hard-coded and no prompt file changed. Tests: two briefs tests, a lib unit test, a budgets test tying rows to `computed_rows()` and checking the verifier frame appears in every verifier set, and a core test via the fake driver. CHANGELOG entry and decision D141 appended.

open_issues: crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs is not on the expected deliverables list; I changed it because it holds the existing fake-driver rig for `ask`, which the reading test needs. A reviewer may flag it as unlisted.

mistakes: The first core test computed tokens left with plain subtraction and panicked, because the stub's two verifier frames overrun the budget. I fixed it with saturating_sub.
learnings: athena-core cannot see the real capabilities (they live in athena-cli wiring), so the core fake-driver test uses the stub capability, whose sections reuse the real frames. The exact real-capability figures are asserted in the CLI budgets test.
